case_analysis.apparent_benchmark_claim: The copied official case materials present a 9-test conjunctive AppWorld task whose ninth registered test is `obtain added, updated, removed todoist.Task records using models.changed_records, and assert 0 were updated.`
case_analysis.actual_checked_outcome: The retained released evaluator outputs show a different ninth registered test was actually used for these runs: `obtain added, updated, removed todoist.Task records using models.changed_records, and assert updated tasks have only changed at most in the order_index field.` That alternate test directly fed `tracker.success` and thus the released label.
case_analysis.target_construction_review: `Task.load` and `GroundTruth.load` bind the run to task-local `evaluation.py` and `test_data.json`. The copied `official/ground_truth/*` files say test 009 is `assert 0 were updated`, but all three retained native evaluator outputs serialize a different test-009 requirement, so the released task-local target construction differed from the copied official case packet.
case_analysis.evaluator_oracle_review: `TestTracker` records only `with test(requirement)` blocks, and its serialized passes/failures preserve the exact requirement text. The retained outputs therefore show that the released oracle actually registered a different ninth requirement than the copied official evaluator/test-data pair.
case_analysis.reward_wiring_aggregation_review: The official worker serializes the exact `TestTracker` returned by `evaluate_task`, sets `run_summary.success` from `tracker.success`, and the post-score join maps `native_evaluator_output.json::tracker.success` to the released label. `Metric` only aggregates after the fact and does not change an individual record’s success. The different ninth test therefore changes the released record outcome through the normal benchmark wiring, not through a separate reward predicate.

official_benchmark_assessment.description: The copied official case artifacts misdescribe the released task semantics. The packet/checklist freeze test 009 as `assert 0 were updated`, but the retained released evaluator outputs for all three records show that the actual task-local evaluator/test-data pair registered a different ninth test about updated tasks changing only `order_index`.

checklist_and_case_packet_assessment.description: The frozen checklist and case packet reproduce the copied official ninth test (`assert 0 were updated`) rather than the released evaluator semantics evidenced in the retained records, so they misstate the benchmark’s native semantics for this case.

records.different_outcome_description: The apparent benchmark claim says test 009 is satisfied exactly when `models.changed_records("todoist.Task")` yields zero updated records. This retained released evaluator output instead shows a different test 009, `assert updated tasks have only changed at most in the order_index field`, and it failed this record on an empty-updated-set assertion.
records.reason: The copied official case files and our frozen checklist claim a zero-updates ninth test, but this exact retained record’s native evaluator output/report serialize a different ninth requirement under `TestTracker`. Because the official worker and join wire `tracker.success` directly to the released label, this record was judged against a different outcome than the benchmark appeared to claim, even though the final released label is also `fail`.
